column3: resfuzz finds crashes, hangs and deadline misses in QNX resource managers.
On QNX, drivers and services are resource managers. Every client reaches them by message passing. resfuzz attacks that interface on the real operating system.
One script builds a QEMU target, boots it headless under TCG, and waits for SSH.
The agent runs on QNX next to the server. It mutates open, read, write, dev control and raw messages, with coverage feedback.
It uses native message passing, Clock Cycles for deadlines, Timer Timeout for hangs, and dumper cores for backtraces.
Ten minutes in, all four planted bugs: a deadline miss, a null dereference, a hang, and a stateful overflow.
The overflow only happens after admin mode. resfuzz recorded two hundred and seventy-one messages and shrank them to two. They crash a fresh server every time.
Every crash and hang comes with a dumper core and a backtrace through QNX's own resource manager layer.
Pointed at the SDP's own P-T-Y driver, it found nothing, and says so.
That honesty matters. Public QNX advisories have documented resource manager bugs in the field. Teams can drop in their own server and run the same loop.
An optional AI step proposes seeds. A validator keeps command numbers from the target, never from the model.
Open source, with a one-hour code lab. resfuzz.
